policy_name: Guide on the use of generative artificial intelligence
regulatory_regime: Government of Canada policy suite on digital government and responsible AI

key_dates.event: Second version published incorporating stakeholder and expert feedback (BT48-37/2024E/F)
canada.ca page reportedly shows 'Date modified' 2026-09-24 (search result only; nature of change unverified)

covered_systems: generative AI tools (GC-managed and publicly available)
covered_activities: use of generative AI by employees
deployment of generative AI tools by institutions
conditions: Directive on Automated Decision-Making applies where generative AI is used for administrative decisions
objective: Provides preliminary guidance to federal institutions on the responsible use of generative AI, describing its risks and setting out best practices (FASTER principles) for employees and institutions.
conflict_rule: Guide does not replace binding instruments; the Privacy Act, Policy on Government Security and Directive on Automated Decision-Making continue to apply and prevail.

record_provenance.notes: canada.ca and publications.gc.ca were blocked by the compilation environment's network policy; clauses are paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false) from knowledge of the second version. Second version publication date 2024-02-12 per publications.gc.ca catalogue; first version Sept 2023 (exact day not verified). A search result indicates the canada.ca page was modified on 2026-09-24, but whether this is a substantive third version could not be verified — check the live page. parent_policy 'Policy on Service and Digital' is an inference about the policy suite, not verified as stated in the guide. CA_AIDA_C27 never became law (bill died); listed only as related Canadian AI context. binding=false: the guide is non-mandatory guidance; status 'voluntary' chosen as closest value.

clauses.original_text: To maintain public trust and ensure the responsible use of generative AI tools, federal institutions should align with the 'FASTER' principles: Fair, Accountable, Secure, Transparent, Educated and Relevant.
clauses.requirement: use generative AI in a way that is fair, accountable, secure, transparent, educated and relevant
clauses.purpose: maintain public trust in government use of generative AI
clauses.affected_asset: public trust; clients of government services
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used by federal institutions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase: canada.ca and publications.gc.ca could not be fetched from the compilation environment, so wording is reconstructed from knowledge of the second version (Feb 2024) of the guide; not verbatim, section headings descriptive. FASTER acronym recalled with high confidence.

clauses.section: Secure: privacy and security best practices
clauses.original_text: Do not enter sensitive or personal information, or protected or classified information, into generative AI tools that are not managed by the Government of Canada.
clauses.object: personal, sensitive, protected or classified information
clauses.requirement: do not input personal, protected or classified information into public/non-GC-managed generative AI tools
clauses.purpose: protect privacy and government information security
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools not managed by the GC
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase: canada.ca and publications.gc.ca could not be fetched from the compilation environment, so wording is reconstructed from knowledge of the second version (Feb 2024) of the guide; not verbatim, section headings descriptive.

clauses.original_text: Identify content that has been produced using generative AI, and notify users when they are interacting with an AI tool; document decisions and be able to provide explanations if tools are used to support decision-making.
clauses.requirement: mark AI-generated content and inform users they are interacting with AI
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools used by federal institutions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase: canada.ca and publications.gc.ca could not be fetched from the compilation environment, so wording is reconstructed from knowledge of the second version (Feb 2024) of the guide; not verbatim, section headings descriptive.

clauses.original_text: Take responsibility for content generated by these tools, including ensuring that it is factual, legal, ethical and compliant with the terms of use, and establish monitoring and oversight mechanisms.
clauses.requirement: verify generated content for accuracy, legality and ethics and remain accountable for it
clauses.affected_asset: quality and lawfulness of government communications and decisions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase: canada.ca and publications.gc.ca could not be fetched from the compilation environment, so wording is reconstructed from knowledge of the second version (Feb 2024) of the guide; not verbatim, section headings descriptive.

clauses.section: Fair / Relevant: assessing risks before deployment
clauses.original_text: Federal institutions should evaluate generative AI tools for their potential risks (including bias, privacy, security and intellectual property risks) before deploying them, consult relevant stakeholders such as legal services, privacy and security experts, and use generative AI only where it is relevant and appropriate for the task.
clauses.action: assess risks and consult before deploying
clauses.recipient: legal, privacy, security and other relevant experts
clauses.requirement: assess risks and consult appropriate experts before deploying generative AI, and use it only where appropriate
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools deployed by federal institutions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase: canada.ca and publications.gc.ca could not be fetched from the compilation environment, so wording is reconstructed from knowledge of the second version (Feb 2024) of the guide; not verbatim, section headings descriptive.

clauses.original_text: Where generative AI is used to make or support administrative decisions about clients, the requirements of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making apply, including completing an Algorithmic Impact Assessment.
clauses.requirement: apply the Directive on Automated Decision-Making when generative AI is used in administrative decisions
clauses.condition: generative AI used to make or assist administrative decisions affecting clients
clauses.purpose: procedural fairness and accountability in automated decisions
clauses.affected_asset: rights and interests of clients subject to administrative decisions
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI used in administrative decision-making
